limitations: These are diagnostic cross-generator comparisons, not replacements for the original 27-case matrix.

redis-benchmark uses 12-digit zero-padded suffixes; the other clients use a fixed zero prefix plus an unpadded integer. 90% of key names match; small indices have shorter keys. Each generator uses the same fixture across all engines.

SET/HSET payload sizes match, but redis-benchmark changes a numeric suffix, memtier mutates randomized binary data, and dfly_bench generates fresh randomized binary data. Write-byte patterns and PRNGs are not identical across generators.
All clients use closed-loop load with coordinated omission. Native latency fields are retained, not pooled across clients.
Client CPU includes startup/shutdown; native throughput excludes some of that overhead. DFly client waits for its progress fiber after its measured interval.

CPU capacity sweep jointly changes threads and CPU affinity: 2 threads/2 CPUs, 4/4, 8/6; always 32 total connections and four server CPUs. VM CPU IDs do not establish physical M4 performance-core affinity.
ZADD scores have the same numeric range, but redis-benchmark uses 12-digit decimal text and memtier uses unpadded decimal text.

redis-benchmark 8.2.1 checks multithreaded completion on a 250-ms timer; up to three calibration extensions target 2.5s and stop at >=2s, capped at 16777216 requests. Measured counts retain 15% headroom and a 40-million cap. Quantization and duration misses remain visible; no measured sample is discarded.
Pipeline depth is the same outstanding-request cap, not a guarantee of identical client batching or refill behavior.
INFO commandstats counters are verified where available (Redis and Dragonfly); ffkv does not expose these counters in this configuration. All INCR runs separately verify the full counter-sum delta.
